QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_49

question.text: AIFs are required to bring an 'Investor Charter' to the notice of their investors. Which of the following BEST describes the Investor Charter?

answer.text: A confidential internal compliance checklist reviewed only by the Trustee.
A document with details of services provided to investors, grievance redressal mechanism and responsibilities of investors, collated in one single place for ease of reference.
A marketing brochure prepared by distributors for client acquisition.
An investor vote-counting register for LP resolutions.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 289): the Investor Charter is a document containing details of the services provided to investors, the grievance redressal mechanism, and the responsibilities of investors, brought together in a single document for ease of reference. Pages 189-190 confirm the disclosure mechanism: for new schemes the Investor Charter is disclosed through the PPM, and for existing schemes it is disclosed once via the investor's registered email. The Trap: Option A wrongly recasts the Charter as internal and confidential. Option C reframes it as marketing collateral. Option D invents a vote-counting register that is not part of the Charter. Note: Disclosure mode is PPM (new schemes) or registered email (existing schemes), per pages 189-190. No website-posting or subscription-booklet requirement is set out in the workbook.
